overall: The AG found the Gardner City Council violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to review executive session minutes at reasonable intervals for continued nondisclosure, while rejecting the complainant's timeliness-of-approval theory.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Council did not release executive session minutes in a timely fashion; the AG treated this as a failure to periodically review those minutes for continued nondisclosure.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the Council failed to review executive session minutes at reasonable intervals to determine whether continued nondisclosure was warranted, in violation of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complainant relied on the 940 CMR 29.11(2) timeliness rule to argue executive session minutes had to be approved or released within a set period.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we do not require that a public body approve executive session minutes within three meetings or 30 days.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law's requirements, including periodic review of executive session minutes at reasonable intervals to determine whether continued nondisclosure is warranted.
remedy_passage: We order immediate and future compliance with the law’s requirements and we caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
